artworks.title: Hypnos and Thanatos Carry Sarpedon (Euphronios Krater)
artworks.description: Euphronios' calyx-krater — Sleep and Death lifting Zeus' Lycian son from the Trojan plain under Hermes' eye — remains the definitive image of Sarpedon's fall.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Books XII and XVI — the rain of blood, Patroclus' spear, and Zeus deciding not to save his own son.

popCulture.title: Euphronios Krater
popCulture.description: The Sarpedon krater — once Met, now Cerveteri — made the Lycian hero modern archaeology's most famous corpse.

popCulture.title: Sarpedon
popCulture.description: Zeus' mortal son who dies at Troy — the Iliad's lesson that even a god's child is not exempt from fate.
